guia.what: A code block with a language label and a copy button. The text is the block’s content. It doesn’t apply syntax highlighting on its own, which keeps the package light and dependency-free.
whenUse: You’re showing a snippet the reader will copy and paste.
It’s a multi-line block, like a command, a config file, or a snippet.
It helps to say what language it’s in.
The same code has alternatives (CDN or npm): the tabs go in the block’s header, not above it.
whenAvoid: It’s a prop or file name inside a sentence → `inline-code`.
It’s a key or a shortcut → `kbd`.
dos: Keep the block copyable. That’s why the button exists.
Show the smallest snippet that makes sense on its own.
donts: Don’t paste whole files when ten lines will do.
Don’t use it to highlight text that isn’t code.

teclado.action: Only with tabs in the header: they switch to the next, previous, first, and last tab, as in Tabs.

nucleo: The copy button confirms the action with brief feedback, and Core handles that. Copies the text to the clipboard and shows the confirmation for 2 seconds—the “Copied” name (`data-ts-copied-label`) and the ✓ (`<template data-ts-copied-icon>`). Then it returns to rest. Pressing it again restarts the 2 seconds.
